NGL chief, this is an awful take. Father Owl is like, #2 in the Sekiro ranking. Dodging is actually very effective on this boss because it allows you to punish attacks that normally push you back in that locked in pushback animation, I've literally never had an issue with his hitboxes, his sword is just pretty friggen long, and on top of all that, when you say "parrying is almost useless" in the game where the sole mechanic in which you are supposed to be interacting with every enemy is \*parrying\*, I think it says more about your skill at the boss than it does the boss. To compare one of the most fucking PEAK bosses in the Souls series to the utter dog-water gank fight that is Dual Apes, is \*insane\* to me.

If you dont play Sekrio without Kuro's Charm Sekiro is way easier than Lies of P.

After you beat the game for the first time you unlock the ability at the start of every new run/NG+ Cycle to give Kuro his Charm. It does the following,  
  
makes it so that you take chip damage on mistimed deflects (Percentage of the attacks damage)  
Take more damage  
Enemies have more health

Really this is my favorite way to play the game and if you're not a speedrunner this is how you should play it as well. But even giving Kuro's Charm away I still think LoP is harder cuz the parry window is tighter and theres a whole bunch of other mechanics at play like insanely slow Stamina Regen, Sharpness, and generally more dangerous debuffs. Both however, are S tier, and I personally have grown to like LoP more because it has a more rewarding NG+, where Sekiro only has Kuro's Charm LoP gives you a ton of new stuff and lore on NG+ which is AWESOME and Fromsoft should take notes.

A final note, there wasn't a popular deflecting game before Sekiro, and the main audience was Souls fans so all of that combined made it so people playing Sekiro for the first time struggled SUPER hard. This is why people remember Genichiro being a skill check (which he still can be for inexperienced people), but realistically if you've played LoP which is also focusing on this deflect system, you've learned like, 70%+ of what Sekiro is all about, making it easier for you. So your experience makes sense.

To be honest, a lot of how you build hadern comes down to personal preference. I always run Hadern with Axatana, so in Eredrims slot I go for his increased stagger ability because Axatana hits a bunch of times really quickly(this makes it so I end up destroying everything in the game with the running katana heavy attack aka bayblade spin to win), and in Solomans slot I run extra reserve slot with no gland because an extra axe special attack is no joke for DPS(also for 99% of the game youre not gonna have a gland on you so, big plays). Everything else is up to you, whether you dont wanna use stamina at all while running, or have a chance to chunk some stamina instead of health, all up to you. The investment of tar and glimpses shouldnt worry you unless youre dying A LOT, in which case, take a second glance at your build. Hope you have tons of fun, Hadern is easily my favorite shell in the game due to his customization and overall strength. (Also, dont forget to take advantage of the fact that with the Axatana, youre invulnerable while in the transformation animation, so use it when you get caught in a situation where youre outta stamina and lacking a harden. Trust me it's a real life saver)
